records.name: Mount Takao
records.description: A 599-meter mountain on the western edge of Hachioji with eight hiking trails, a cable car, and a chairlift. It draws more than 2.5 million visitors a year, making it one of the most-climbed mountains in the world, and is known for old-growth cedar forest, over 1,200 plant species, and autumn foliage. Yakuoin Temple sits near the summit.

tips.text: Trail 1 is the main paved route to the summit and can be shortened with the cable car or chairlift partway up.
The mountain has eight numbered trails of varying difficulty; hiking to the top on foot takes about 90 minutes on average.

records.station: Takaosanguchi Station (Keio Takao Line) / Takao Station (JR Chuo Line)
records.address: 高尾山　大見晴園地, 稲荷山線歩道, 八王子市, 東京都, 193-0841

records.name: Takaosan Yakuoin Yukiji (Yakuoin Temple)
records.description: A Shingon Buddhist temple near the summit of Mount Takao, founded in 744 on the order of Emperor Shomu with the priest Gyoki associated with its founding. It was restored in the late 14th century by the priest Shungen and is one of three head temples of the Chizan school of Shingon Buddhism, known for its tengu statues and waterfall ascetic training.

tips.text: Waterfall ascetic training (takigyo) is held at the Ja-taki and Biwa-taki waterfalls on set dates each month; call ahead to confirm times if you want to observe or participate.
From Takaosanguchi Station, reach the temple via the cable car (Kiyotaki to Takaosan) or the chairlift, followed by about a 20-minute walk.

records.name: Mt. Takao Cable Car (Takaotozan Railway)
records.description: A funicular railway linking Kiyotaki Station at the base of Mount Takao with Takaosan Station partway up the mountain, opened in 1927. The roughly 1,020-meter track has a maximum gradient of about 31 degrees, among the steepest of any railway in Japan. A parallel chairlift covers the same stretch of mountain.

tips.text: The cable car and a parallel chairlift both connect the mountain base to the Kasumidai area near the monkey park, cutting significant time off the hike to Yakuoin Temple and the summit.

records.station: Kiyotaki Station, near Takaosanguchi Station (Keio Takao Line)

records.name: Takao 599 Museum
records.description: A free nature museum at the base of Mount Takao focused on the mountain's flora and fauna, with taxidermy displays, insects and wildflowers set in acrylic resin, an indoor cafe, and an outdoor lawn area.

tips.text: Admission is free, though a paid area and special exhibitions may carry separate fees.

records.name: Takao Monkey Park and Wild Plant Garden
records.description: A combined Japanese macaque park and wild plant garden on Trail 1 of Mount Takao. The monkey park introduces the resident troop's family tree and history of successive leader monkeys, while the adjoining garden displays seasonal native flora with rotating bloom information.

tips.text: Admission is 500 yen for adults and 250 yen for children.

records.hours: Seasonal, approximately 9:30 AM-4:30 PM, last admission 15 minutes before closing
records.station: 3-minute walk from the Mt. Takao cable car mountain station

records.name: Kasumidai Observatory
records.description: An observation deck near the upper cable car and chairlift stations on Mount Takao, close to the monkey park. It offers views toward Yokohama and, on clear days, Mount Fuji and the Tokyo skyline.

tips.text: From Kasumidai it is about a 15-minute walk to Yakuoin Temple and around 40 minutes to the summit.

records.station: Reached via the Mt. Takao cable car or chairlift from Takaosanguchi Station

records.name: Biwa Waterfall (Biwa-taki)
records.description: A waterfall about a third of the way up Trail 6 on Mount Takao, used by Yakuoin Temple as a site for waterfall ascetic training (takigyo). The falls themselves are gated off from general visitors, who can view them from behind the closed gate; entry is limited to trainees on scheduled dates.

tips.text: Waterfall training at Biwa-taki is scheduled for the first Saturday of the month plus the 18th and 28th; call the temple ahead to confirm.

records.name: Ja-taki Waterfall
records.description: One of two waterfalls on Mount Takao used by Yakuoin Temple for waterfall ascetic training, reached from the Jyataki-guchi bus stop. Like Biwa-taki, it is a working training site rather than a general sightseeing spot.

tips.text: Waterfall training at Ja-taki is scheduled for the first Saturday of the month plus the 17th and 27th; call the temple ahead to confirm times.

records.name: Tako Sugi (Octopus Cedar)
records.description: A large cedar tree on Trail 1 of Mount Takao, estimated at more than 450 years old, named for exposed roots that curve outward like an octopus's tentacles.

records.name: Miyama-bashi Suspension Bridge
records.description: A suspension bridge on Trail 4 of Mount Takao, described as the only suspension bridge on the mountain. The trail passes through deciduous forest along a route roughly 1.5 kilometers long.

records.name: Takao Visitor Center
records.description: A free nature information center near the summit of Mount Takao with staff and nature guides who provide information on the mountain's trails, plants, and wildlife.

records.name: Keio Takaosan Onsen Gokurakuyu
records.description: A hot spring bathhouse next to Takaosanguchi Station at the base of Mount Takao, with indoor and outdoor baths, saunas, and a relaxation area, aimed at hikers coming off the mountain.
records.station: Adjacent to Takaosanguchi Station (Keio Takao Line)

records.name: Takao Baigo Plum Grove
records.description: A series of plum groves strung along roughly 5 kilometers of the old Koshu Kaido road on the north side of Mount Takao, including the Sekisho, Tenjin, Yunohana, Kogesawa, and Keoroshizawa sections. About 10,000 plum trees bloom here from mid-February to late March, with a plum festival held around March 10.

tips.text: Take a bus bound for Kobotoke from Takao Station and get off at Ohshimo to reach the Kogesawa plum grove section; there is no parking at the site.

records.station: Takao Station (JR Chuo Line / Keio Takao Line), then bus

records.name: Hachioji Castle Ruins
records.description: The ruins of a mountaintop Sengoku-period castle built in 1587 by Hojo Ujiteru of the Late Hojo clan. Toyotomi Hideyoshi's forces captured and destroyed it in a single day on June 23, 1590, during the campaign against the Hojo. The site has partial reconstructions from 1990, including stone walls, a bridge, and the lord's palace entrance, and has been a National Historic Site since 1951, with protection expanded in 2005. It is included among the Japan Castle Foundation's Top 100 Castles.

tips.text: From JR Takao Station, take the Nishi Tokyo Bus to the Reienmae/Hachiojijoseki-iriguchi stop, then walk about 20 minutes to the ruins.

records.station: Takao Station (JR Chuo Line), then bus
records.address: 国史跡八王子城跡案内図, かつら南門通り, 八王子市, 東京都, 193-0826

records.name: Takiyama Castle Ruins
records.description: The ruins of a hilltop Sengoku-period castle in the Tani neighborhood of Hachioji, built by Oishi Sadashige in 1521 and later associated with the samurai Hojo Ujiteru. The earthworks and moat follow the natural shape of the hill, with a reconstructed bridge between the Honmaru and Nakanomaru enclosures. The site has been a National Historic Site since 2007 and was named one of the Continued Top 100 Japanese Castles in 2017.

records.name: Musashi Imperial Graveyard
records.description: An Imperial mausoleum complex in the Nagabusa-machi area of Hachioji, established in 1926, that holds the mausolea of Emperor Taisho, Empress Teimei, Emperor Showa, and Empress Kojun. The grounds are a semi-natural cedar forest with wide gravel approach roads and a zelkova-lined sando, and Emperor Taisho was the first Japanese emperor buried in the Tokyo area rather than Kyoto.

tips.text: The graveyard is reached from the north exit of JR and Keio Takao Station.

records.station: Takao Station (JR Chuo Line / Keio Takao Line), north exit

records.name: Tokyo Fuji Art Museum
records.description: An art museum near Soka University in Hachioji, opened November 3, 1983, with a collection of more than 30,000 works spanning Japanese, Eastern, and Western art, including paintings, prints, photography, sculpture, ceramics, lacquerware, armor, and swords. It is known for a Western oil painting collection covering roughly 500 years, from the Renaissance to contemporary periods, and has held exchanges with institutions in 32 countries and regions.

tips.text: General admission is 1,500 yen; last entry is 30 minutes before closing.

records.hours: 10:00 AM-5:00 PM, Tuesday-Sunday and holidays; closed Mondays and New Year holidays
records.station: Hachioji Station (JR Chuo, Yokohama, Hachiko Lines), then 1-minute walk from Soka University main gate

records.name: Tama Forest Science Garden
records.description: A 57-hectare arboretum at the foot of Mount Takao, formerly the Asakawa Experiment Forest, run as a branch of the Forestry and Forest Products Research Institute since being founded in 1921. It holds an arboretum of about 500 tree species alongside a Cherry Tree Preservation Forest of roughly 1,800 to 2,000 cherry trees across 250 cultivated varieties, some descended from Edo-period stock.

tips.text: The garden is closed on Mondays and New Year holidays; last entry is 30 minutes before closing.

records.hours: 9:30 AM-4:00 PM, Tuesday-Sunday and holidays; closed Mondays and New Year holidays
records.station: Takao Station (JR Chuo Line / Keio Takao Line), about 10-minute walk from the North Exit

records.name: Icho Namiki (Koshu Kaido Ginkgo Avenue)
records.description: A roughly 4-kilometer stretch of the Koshu Kaido road in Hachioji lined with several hundred ginkgo trees, planted in 1929 to commemorate construction of the nearby Tama Imperial Mausoleum. The trees turn gold from mid-November to early December, and the annual Hachioji Ginkgo Festival is held along the avenue in that period.

tips.text: The avenue runs from the Oiwakecho intersection to in front of Takao Station; a bus from Hachioji Station to the Namiki-cho stop, about 15 minutes, puts you within a short walk.

records.station: Namiki-cho bus stop, about 15 minutes from Hachioji Station

records.name: Mount Jinba
records.description: A mountain on the Tokyo-Kanagawa border, straddling Hachioji and Sagamihara, with a peak generally cited around 855-857 meters. It is a popular hiking destination valued for its views toward Mount Fuji, though reaching it from central Hachioji requires roughly an hour by bus.

records.name: Komiya Park
records.description: A woodland park on Kasumi Hill in Hachioji with oak and cherry trees, a pond, Shinto shrines, and a Buddhist temple within its grounds, connected by wooden walkways across varied elevation. It hosts seasonal nature classes and viewing tours.

records.name: Naganuma Park
records.description: A 313,486-square-meter park created in 1980 on the north slope of the Tama Hills, with broad-leaved woodland of sawtooth and jolcham oak, about 100 meters of elevation change, and an observation platform on the Yaen Ridge Trail overlooking Hachioji and the Okutama mountains.

tips.text: The park is about a 5-minute walk from Naganuma Station on the Keio Line.

records.name: Mt. Inari (Inariyama Trail)
records.description: A minor 396-meter peak on the Inariyama Trail approaching Mount Takao, notable for seasonal wildflowers including hydrangea and lilies along the route.

records.name: Iroha no Mori Trail
records.description: A roughly 1.5-kilometer trail on Mount Takao planted with 48 tree species, one for each character of the traditional Japanese iroha syllabary, with poetry inscriptions posted alongside the trees.
